a101877_a9_verified.txt
=======================

OEIS A101877, n = 9.   RESULT:  a(9) = 8498.

Status: proved.  An explicit set attains 8498 (Sections 4-5), and two independently checked
certificates exclude every set whose largest element is at most 8497 (Section 6).


1. Definition
-------------

A101877:  a(n) = min { max(S) : S a finite set of distinct positive integers,
                                 sum_{x in S} 1/x = n }.

So a(9) = 8498 means:
  (a) there is a set S of distinct positive integers with max(S) = 8498 and sum 1/x = 9, and
  (b) no set of distinct positive integers with largest element <= 8497 has sum 1/x = 9.

OEIS lists 1, 6, 24, 65, 184, 469, 1243, 3231 for n = 1..8.  (Side remark: earlier work in this
repository, re-checked here, has an exact witness with largest element 3228 for n = 8, and a
certificate that nothing with largest element <= 3227 exists.  So a(8) = 3228, and the listed
3231 is too large.)


2. Summary of the proof
-----------------------

  upper bound  a(9) <= 8498 :  the explicit 5966-element set S of Section 4; its reciprocal sum
                               is exactly 9 (Section 5, four independent exact checks).
  lower bound  a(9) >= 8498 :  (i)  no S in [1..8496] has sum 9    (certificate, Section 6);
                               (ii) no S with max(S) = 8497 has sum 9 (certificate, Section 6).

Both certificates are checked by verify_cert.py.  That script recomputes everything from scratch
with exact integer arithmetic and shares no code with the C++ solvers.


3. Previously established bounds, and what is new here
------------------------------------------------------

Before this work (earlier sessions in this repository):
  * a(9) <= 8500: a witness with max 8500 (a second one has max 8502); both re-verified here.
  * No S in [1..8496]: a root-closure certificate, independently verified.
  * No S with max 8497: a branch-and-bound run (239 nodes) without an independent certificate.
  * 8499 = 3*2833 and 8501 (a prime) cannot be the maximum of any set with integral sum.
    For 8499 the only possible multiples of 2833 are 2833, 5666 and 8499.  None of the four
    subsets of {1, 2, 3} that contain 3 has a reciprocal sum whose numerator is divisible by 2833.
  * So 8498 <= a(9) <= 8500.  Only 8498 was undecided: the previous solver stopped after about
    38,300 nodes (82 minutes) without a decision.

New here:
  * A witness with max 8498, found by the revised solver after 67 search nodes (37 s, one core).
  * The case max = 8497 now has a root-closure certificate (1 node, 1.7 s, independently verified).
    The previous solver needed 239 nodes and produced no certificate.
  * The case S in [1..8496] was re-proved by the revised solver with a 100x larger margin.  The new
    certificate is independently verified; the old certificate is also re-verified.
Hence a(9) = 8498.

In the exclusion form of Section 7, sum_{x in E} 1/x = sum_{x in U} 1/x - 9 = Delta, where

5. Exact verification of the construction
-----------------------------------------

Every listed denominator was checked:
  * every entry is a positive integer;
  * the 5966 entries are pairwise distinct;
  * the smallest is 1 and the largest is 8498 (so max(S) = 8498 exactly).

The reciprocal sum was checked to be exactly 9 in four independent ways:
  (1) Python fractions.Fraction (exact rationals):  sum_{x in S} Fraction(1, x) == 9.
  (2) Pure integer identity.  With L = lcm(S), a 384-digit integer,
        sum_{x in S} L/x  ==  9 * L      (every L/x is an exact integer division).
      L = 19994249832384148862215211221470120843195785436911323553775551391699493048299699
      86182663099335697022021035009043878031974873295137864357652399305503299791703205
      82833654516737447019216396948799936405365159481025376393093250863101916998357373
      00259043493800737607042900805518158910699824070308672643466905417071629474579166
      3735440813982194687041872422565920941333255164755665809885440000
  (3) sympy.Rational:  the sum is 9.
  (4) C++ (a101877_v2 check 9 8498 ..., and the previous solver's check mode).  For every prime
      p <= 8498, sum_{x in S, p|x} c_p(x) == 0 (mod p^E), so the sum has no prime in its
      denominator and is an integer (Rule 1 of Section 7).  Exact integer fixed-point bounds,
      floor(2^48/x) and ceil(2^48/x) summed over S, place it strictly between 8 and 10.  So it is 9.

Correction check of the earlier examples.  All ten witness files from the earlier work (n = 1..9,
including the max-8500 and max-8502 sets for n = 9) were re-checked in the same way: distinct
positive integers, the stated maximum, and an exact reciprocal sum n.  All are correct; no
corrections were needed.  The construction above is new, not a modification of those files.


6. Optimality: no set with largest element <= 8497
--------------------------------------------------

Notation.  For a prime p <= K, let p^E be the largest power of p with p^E <= K.  For p | x <= K,
  c_p(x) = p^(E - v_p(x)) * (x / p^v_p(x))^(-1)  mod p^E,
so c_p(x)/p^E is the p-part of the partial-fraction expansion of 1/x.

Certificate argument (Rules 1-4 of Section 7).  Let U be the candidate set and
Delta = sum_U 1/x - 9.  If some S had sum 9, then E = U \ S would satisfy:
  res_p(E) := sum_{x in E, p|x} c_p(x) == R_p := res_p(U)  (mod p^E)  for every prime p, and
  sum_{x in E} 1/x = Delta.
A certificate lists integer weights lam[p][x] for the pairs (prime p, x in U with p | x), with
sum_p lam[p][x] <= floor(2^48 / x) for every x.  Then for that E:
  2^48 * Delta = 2^48 * sum_E 1/x >= sum_{x in E} floor(2^48/x) >= sum_p sum_{x in E, p|x} lam[p][x]
              >= sum_p m_p,
where m_p = min { sum_{x in T} lam[p][x] : T a set of multiples of p in U, res_p(T) == R_p }.
The last step holds because E's multiples of p form one such T.  Each m_p is an exact finite
minimum (dynamic programming over residues mod p^E).  If sum_p m_p > Dhi, where
Dhi := sum_U ceil(2^48/x) - 9 * 2^48 >= 2^48 * Delta, this is a contradiction.  So no S exists.
In "forced-in" form (the claim "no S containing K"), K may not be in E, so it is excluded from
every T.

  Certificate                            claim                          |U|   sum_p m_p - Dhi
  certificates/cert_n9_K8496_v2.txt      no S in [1..8496], sum 9       6326  19,327,643,490 > 0
  certificates/cert_n9_K8496.txt (old)   no S in [1..8496], sum 9       6326     191,468,360 > 0
  certificates/cert_n9_K8497w.txt        no S with max(S) = 8497        6327   4,008,227,003 > 0
  (units of 2^-48; checked by: verify_cert.py <file> [--forced-in 8497], or verify_a9.py)

verify_cert.py recomputes, from scratch and with integer arithmetic only: the candidate set U, the
residues R_p, Dhi, the split condition, and every m_p (a plain residue DP, not the level DP of the
solver).  A set with largest element <= 8497 is either contained in [1..8496] or has largest
element 8497, so both cases are covered and a(9) >= 8498.  Bounds used: only these two
certificates.  The old certificate for [1..8496] is re-verified, and the case 8497 is now
certified rather than resting on an uncertified branch-and-bound run.  The values 8499 and 8500
play no role in the final result.


7. The algorithm (a101877/a101877_v2.cpp) and why every reduction is sound
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Input: n and K.  Mode "prove" asks whether some S in [1..K] has sum n.  Mode "witness" asks
whether such an S contains K, i.e. max(S) = K.  All arithmetic is on 64/128-bit integers; there
is no floating point anywhere.

Rule 1 (p-adic integrality).  A finite sum of 1/x with x <= K is an integer iff, for every prime
  p <= K, sum_{x in S, p|x} c_p(x) == 0 (mod p^E).
  Why: write x = p^v r with p not dividing r and v <= E.  Then 1/x = p^(E-v) r^(-1) / p^E plus a
  p-integral number.  So the p-adic valuation of the sum is >= 0 iff p^E divides the sum of the
  c_p(x).  No other primes can occur in the denominators.

Rule 2 (candidate filter).  Delete x if, for some prime p | x, no set of the remaining multiples
  of p that contains x has residue 0 mod p^E.  Repeat until nothing changes.
  Why no solution is lost: if x is in a valid S, then S's multiples of p form such a set for
  every p | x.  By induction over the deletion rounds, no element of S is ever deleted.
  Effect at K = 8498: 8498 numbers shrink to |U| = 6328, and no multiple of a prime > 1019
  survives.  The same rule shows that 8499 and 8501 can never be the largest element.

Rule 3 (exclusion form and integrality).  For S in U put E = U \ S.  Then S has sum n iff E is
  "residue-fixing" (res_p(E) == R_p for all p) and sum_E 1/x = Delta.
  For every residue-fixing E, sum_E 1/x - Delta = n - sum_S 1/x is an integer.  So a solution
  has cost exactly Delta, and any proven lower bound > Delta on the cost of every residue-fixing
  E of a subproblem closes that subproblem.  At K = 8498, Delta = 0.06964..., so E is a
  very light set; in the witness, |E| = 362 and min(E) = 1282.

Rule 4 (Lagrangian lower bound).  The certificate argument of Section 6, at every search node,
  with the node's fixings imposed inside each per-prime minimum (forced-in elements must be in
  T, forced-out elements must not).  It is valid for any integer weights.  The weights only
  affect the strength of the bound, never its correctness.
  Efficient representation: m_p is computed by a DP over the p-adic levels.  An element of
  valuation v adds a multiple of p^(E-v), so it changes only the top v base-p digits.  Once all
  elements of valuation >= v+1 are processed, digit E-v-1 is final; it must equal R_p's digit and
  is dropped.  The state at level v therefore has p^v values, not p^E, so one pass over all 150
  primes takes about 3.5 ms on one core at K = 8498.  Costs are fixed-point integers: floor(2^48/x) in the
  bound, and ceil(2^48/x) in Dhi.
  NEW in v2: the multipliers are optimized by a Polyak subgradient with an adaptive target, namely
  the best bound so far plus delta, with delta halved after 30 non-improving steps.  The previous
  solver aimed at a fixed target above Dhi, which stalls at a weaker bound.  Root bound, minus Dhi:
    K = 8497 (witness):  -29,677,051,138 (v1, open)  ->  +4,008,227,003 (v2, closed at the root)
    K = 8498 (witness): -491,330,541,200 (v1)        ->  -372,349,182,797 (v2)

Rule 5 (reduced-cost fixing and propagation).  With forward and backward DP tables, each block
  yields, for every free x, its exact minimum with x forced into T and with x forced out.  Summing
  over the primes dividing x gives valid lower bounds LB_in(x) and LB_out(x) for the subproblem
  with x in E and with x not in E.  If LB_in(x) > Dhi, then x is in S in every solution of the
  node, so it is fixed out of E; symmetrically for LB_out.  If both exceed Dhi, the node is
  closed.  Every fixing is implied by the node's constraints, so no solution is lost.
  NEW in v2: after fixings, the node is re-probed with the same weights until nothing changes;
  the bound can only rise when options are removed.  Then it is re-optimized briefly (40 steps,
  at most 4 times) and probed again.  The previous solver started a full new node after every
  round of fixings.

Rule 6 (branching).  If the per-prime optimal sets agree on every element, their union is a
  residue-fixing E.  If its cost is < Delta + 1, it is a solution (Rule 3; here 0 <= Delta < 1),
  and it is re-verified exactly before output.  Otherwise, branch on an element on which the
  primes disagree, choosing the one whose weaker child bound is largest; the child "x in E" is
  explored first.  The two children fix x in opposite ways, so they partition the node's search
  space.  The search is complete, and it terminates because each branching fixes a new element.

Symmetry breaking.  The problem has no nontrivial symmetry: x -> 1/x is injective, so no two
  candidates are interchangeable.  Each solution is reached by exactly one root-to-leaf path,
  because the branching is a partition.  The structural reductions that matter are Rules 2, 3
  and 5, plus witness mode, which fixes K in S.

Parallelism (optional, threads=T).  Subtrees are shared through a work stack, and the explored
  nodes still partition the space.  threads=1 (the default) is deterministic: the run below
  always returns the same 67-node search and the same witness.

What did not help (kept short for the record):
  * Merging small primes (2, 3) with all large primes (> sqrt K) into joint DP blocks did not
    raise the root bound (-3.730e11 vs -3.723e11).
  * A complete proof by element branching at K = 8498 did not look feasible.  In the first levels
    the bound rose by only 1e9 to 2e10 per level, against a root gap of 3.7e11.  This did not
    matter, because a witness exists.
  * CP-SAT on a linear model (residue equalities with integer slack variables) found no solution:
    neither the known max-8500 solution (about 12 minutes, 1 worker) nor a max-8498 solution
    (about 28 minutes, 2 workers).

Structural observation.  Once every element with a prime factor > sqrt(K) is fixed, the remaining
smooth subproblem is decided at the root in about 0.5 s.  For example, the large-prime layer of
the max-8500 witness cannot be completed at K = 8498: its bound exceeds Dhi by +755,891,295.
The slack of the relaxation therefore sits in the large-prime layer, which is why
"largefirst=1" and neighbourhood restrictions are offered as options.  Neither was needed for
the final run.


8. Search statistics and comparison with the previous algorithm
----------------------------------------------------------------

The decisive run (single core, default options):
  ./a101877_v2 witness 9 8498
  -> FOUND |S| = 5966, nodes = 67, DP passes = 15,847, max depth = 60,
     root LB - Dhi = -372,349,182,797, time = 37 s
     (root optimization 11.5 s, then 66 more nodes)

Comparison on the same machine, one core each (bench_v1_v2.sh; outputs in a101877/bench/).
v1 = previous solver a101877.cpp, v2 = revised a101877_v2.cpp.  "Nodes" for v1 counts every
re-solve after fixings as a node; v2 counts branch-and-bound nodes, with fixing rounds inside
the node.

  instance                         v1 nodes / time               v2 nodes / time
  prove   8 3227  (proof)          1 / 0.20 s                    1 / 0.21 s
  prove   9 8496  (proof)          1 / 1.49 s                    1 / 1.43 s   (margin 100x larger)
  witness 9 8497  (proof)          239 / 45.3 s                  1 / 1.75 s   (root certificate)
  witness 10 22789 (proof)         2 / 22.6 s                    1 / 6.6 s    (root certificate)
  witness 6 469   (find)           19 / 0.11 s                   8 / 0.06 s
  witness 7 1243  (find)           30 / 0.83 s                   14 / 0.72 s
  witness 8 3228  (find)           2722 / 170.4 s                22 / 4.1 s
  witness 9 8500  (find)           3568 / 593.3 s                144 / 60.4 s
  witness 9 8498  (find)           3000 / 424.3 s, not found     67 / 37.4 s
                                   (node cap reached)
  (Earlier logs of v1 with 4 threads: witness 9 8500 found after 3568 nodes, about 30 min;
   witness 9 8498 stopped after about 38,300 nodes and 82 min without a decision.)


9. Reproducing the computation
------------------------------

  cd a101877
  g++ -O2 -march=native -pthread -o a101877_v2 a101877_v2.cpp     # revised solver (no floats)
  g++ -O2 -march=native -pthread -o a101877    a101877.cpp        # previous solver (comparison)

  ./a101877_v2 witness 9 8498                    # finds the witness (67 nodes, about 40 s)
  ./a101877_v2 check 9 8498 "$(cat witnesses/witness_n9_max8498.txt)"
  ./a101877_v2 prove 9 8496 cert=c8496.txt       # root closure; writes the multipliers
  ./a101877_v2 witness 9 8497 cert=c8497.txt     # root closure; writes the multipliers
  python3 verify_cert.py c8496.txt
  python3 verify_cert.py c8497.txt --forced-in 8497
  python3 verify_a9.py                           # all checks of Sections 5-6 in one go (about 2 s)
  ./bench_v1_v2.sh v2 ; ./bench_v1_v2.sh v1_short   # comparison table (and v1_8500, v1_8498)

Requirements: g++ (C++17), Python 3 with numpy (verify_cert.py); sympy only for the optional
third sum check.


10. Files (directory a101877/ of this repository)
--------------------------------------------------

  a101877_v2.cpp                     revised exact solver (this work)
  a101877.cpp                        previous solver (unchanged; used for the comparison)
  witnesses/witness_n9_max8498.txt   the set S of Section 4 (comma separated)
  certificates/cert_n9_K8496_v2.txt  certificate: no S in [1..8496]           (new)
  certificates/cert_n9_K8496.txt     certificate: no S in [1..8496]           (earlier work)
  certificates/cert_n9_K8497w.txt    certificate: no S with max(S) = 8497     (new)
  verify_cert.py, verify_witness.py  independent exact checkers (earlier work, unchanged)
  verify_a9.py                       one-shot verification of a(9) = 8498 (this work)
  bench_v1_v2.sh, bench/*.txt        single-core comparison runs
